Y-axis has labeled ticks at intervals of 400: 0, 400, 800, 1,200, 1,600, 2,000, 2,400, 2,800.
The data line is a solid blue line connecting data points for each year from 2018 to 2023.
The data point for 2018 is at the top of the chart, aligned with the 2,800 mark on the y-axis.
The data point for 2019 is lower than 2018, aligned with the 2,400 mark on the y-axis.

printed_facts.fact: The data point for 2020 is higher than 2019, aligned with the 2,800 mark on the y-axis.
The data point for 2021 is lower than 2020, aligned with the 2,400 mark on the y-axis.
The data point for 2022 is at the same level as 2021, aligned with the 2,400 mark on the y-axis.
The data point for 2023 is at the same level as 2022, aligned with the 2,400 mark on the y-axis.
The chart title 'Increasing River Restoration Capacity from 2018 to 2023' implies a positive trend, but the data shows a decline after 2020.
The x-axis ticks are labeled with years in chronological order from 2018 to 2023.
The y-axis ticks are labeled with Capacity Index values in increments of 400, starting from 0 to 2,800.
The data line connects the data points for each year, showing the trend over time.

public_definitions: Assess the river restoration capacity dashboard for the 2018-2023 review window and send the record to the downstream route that best matches the overall dashboard trend.
Use the dashboard trend as the basis for selecting the most appropriate operational route for this record.
The primary field label is 'River restoration capacity handling route'.

The three options are: 'Route the record to routine restoration capacity monitoring', 'Route the record to restoration capacity expansion follow-up', and 'Route the record to restoration capacity decline response review'.
